INSIGHT: Ned explicitly recognizes that formal ADHD behavioral/observation testing is essentially useless for him. He's spent 25 years unconsciously masking ADHD symptoms — the executive control required to suppress symptoms is so ingrained that when consciously aware of being tested, he can perform neurotypically on demand.

'If I know I'm being tested, what's stopping me from acting however I want? I can mimic the exact symptoms or not. The only valid data is honest self-report.'

IMPLICATION: Self-report + clinical history + modafinil response are the actual diagnostic evidence. Formal observation-based ADHD testing adds little value for someone with his profile.

RELEVANT FOR: Psychiatrist conversations — lean into self-report and pharmacological evidence, don't over-weight formal test scores. The 1-month ADHD assessment may disappoint for this reason.

NOTE: He still plans to attend it as a process step, not because he trusts the output.
